items.criterion: The catch-all collection states a count of one hundred and seventy-four watches over eleven numbered pages.
items.judgment: The count and the page total are read from the collection payload.
items.evidence: The seed holds 174 products and the page size is 16.

items.criterion: The availability facet reports one hundred and sixty-one available watches and thirteen unavailable ones, summing to the stated count.
items.judgment: The two facet counts are read and added.
items.evidence: 161 plus 13 is 174, the catalogue total.

items.criterion: The store holds one hundred and seventy-four product rows, eleven collection rows and a row for every home product.
items.judgment: The declared tables are counted and each seeded title is looked up.
items.evidence: The seed is the catalogue the storefront serves.

items.criterion: The stored availability of the product rows matches the availability facet the collection reports.
items.judgment: The rows are counted by availability and compared with the facet.
items.evidence: A facet computed over other rows would disagree.

items.criterion: Every colourway of a watch is stored with its own price, its own option value and its own availability.
items.judgment: The variant rows of the rebel-face watch are read.
items.evidence: Five colourways, one of them sold out, all at the same price.

items.criterion: A card whose colourways cost different amounts opens From the cheapest colourway a buyer can have.
items.judgment: The card for the diamond-scale watch is read.
items.evidence: The cheapest colourway overall is sold out, so the From price is the next one up.

items.criterion: A card carrying no rating is served with a null rating rather than a reserved blank.
items.judgment: The served cards are partitioned by rating.
items.evidence: At least one catalogue product carries no rating.

items.criterion: The twelve home products are served with the struck-through original, the badges and the rating the brief pins.
items.judgment: Each of the twelve is opened and its compare-at, badges and rating are read.
items.evidence: The pinned table in the brief.

items.criterion: The catalogue carries at least five maker names and titles that do not open with the maker.
items.judgment: The distinct makers and the other-maker titles are read from the rows.
items.evidence: The card must survive a title the maker cannot be parsed out of.

items.criterion: A facet selection and a sort survive in the address and reorder or narrow what the collection serves.
items.judgment: The collection is requested with a facet and with each sort.
items.evidence: A shared address reproduces a narrowed view.

items.criterion: Every sort the storefront offers is accepted and reorders the collection rather than narrowing it.
items.judgment: Each declared sort is requested and the count is compared.
items.evidence: A sort reorders; a facet narrows.

items.criterion: The collection pages by a numbered page parameter, and two pages share no product.
items.judgment: Page one, page seven and the last page are read.
items.evidence: Sixteen products a page over eleven pages.

items.criterion: Two identical collection requests serve the same products and the same facet counts.
items.judgment: One request is repeated and the payloads are compared.
items.evidence: A collection read is deterministic.

items.criterion: A product route serves every colourway with its own price, image seed and availability.
items.judgment: The rebel-face watch payload is read.
items.evidence: Five colourways under the option name the brief pins.

items.criterion: An unavailable colourway stays in the swatch grid with its price and its image.
items.judgment: The sold-out colourway is looked up in the served payload.
items.evidence: Removing it would hide a price a buyer may want.

items.criterion: A watch whose colourways carry two different prices is served with both.
items.judgment: The women's business watch payload is read.
items.evidence: Two colourways, two prices.

items.criterion: Every amount on a route converts to the second display currency by one rate in one pass.
items.judgment: The sale price and the struck-through original are read in both currencies.
items.evidence: One rate of eighty-eight.

items.criterion: One watch costs the same on the collection card and on its own route in one currency.
items.judgment: The card and the detail payload are compared.
items.evidence: Both derive from the same variant rows.

items.criterion: The cart states a unit count that sums the quantities on its lines.
items.judgment: Two colourways are added at quantities two and one.
items.evidence: Three units over two lines.

items.criterion: Cart lines hold the order they were added in when a quantity changes.
items.judgment: A middle line's quantity is raised and the order is re-read.
items.evidence: Insertion order never changes.

items.criterion: A cart survives a reload on the same session token with its lines and its unit count.
items.judgment: A second client reads the cart on the same cookies.
items.evidence: The cart is keyed by a token.

items.criterion: The shipping upsell is an ordinary catalogue product with its own price and struck-through original.
items.judgment: The upsell row and its served payload are read.
items.evidence: One thousand minor units against two thousand.

items.criterion: A cart holding the shipping upsell alone is refused or left empty.
items.judgment: The upsell is added to an empty cart.
items.evidence: A cart of nothing but a fee is an empty cart.

items.criterion: The checkout summary restates the cart line for line, unit for unit and amount for amount.
items.judgment: The cart and the summary are compared.
items.evidence: The summary is derived from the cart.

items.criterion: A completed guest order opens exactly one billing account under the order's own reference.
items.judgment: The billing tenant is polled for the reference.
items.evidence: External keys are unique per tenant.

items.criterion: Re-submitting one order reference leaves exactly one billing account behind it.
items.judgment: The checkout is sent twice with one reference.
items.evidence: The billing store refuses the repeat.

items.criterion: A reference the storefront never issued has no billing account behind it.
items.judgment: An invented reference is looked up.
items.evidence: Accounts are opened by a completed order alone.

items.criterion: A completed order leaves the cart empty.
items.judgment: The cart is read after a checkout.
items.evidence: A cart that survives a purchase re-sells it.

items.criterion: The discount code reaches the address a visitor typed as a real message delivered over the mail transport.
items.judgment: The inbox is searched for the subject the brief pins.
items.evidence: A row is not a message.

items.criterion: A malformed or repeated signup is refused and delivers no further mail.
items.judgment: The inbox count is compared before and after a refusal.
items.evidence: A refusal writes nothing and sends nothing.

items.criterion: A submission carrying the unattended decoy field is refused and stores no row.
items.judgment: The signup table is counted before and after.
items.evidence: The decoy is never shown to a visitor.

items.criterion: One session submitting a form repeatedly in quick succession draws a refusal.
items.judgment: Six submissions are sent in succession.
items.evidence: The brief pins a submission limit.

items.criterion: The contact form records a message and delivers none.
items.judgment: The inbox is compared before and after a contact submission.
items.evidence: Only the signup sends mail.

items.criterion: Every catalogue write is refused as an invalid request and the seeded rows are unchanged.
items.judgment: Six write shapes are sent and the tables are re-counted.
items.evidence: The catalogue is read-only at the server.

items.criterion: Every response carries the declared security headers.
items.judgment: Five routes are read and their headers compared.
items.evidence: The deployment contract pins them.

items.criterion: A facet value outside the declared set draws a client error.
items.judgment: An invented availability value is requested.
items.evidence: A silent ignore would serve the whole collection.

items.criterion: An unknown collection and an unknown watch answer as not found.
items.judgment: Two invented handles are requested.
items.evidence: A four-oh-four is the declared answer.

items.criterion: Page views are recorded and served newest first.
items.judgment: Two routes are opened and the record list is read.
items.evidence: The data model pins the visit table.

items.criterion: The machine-readable route list names every public route.
items.judgment: The route list is read and searched for each public route.
items.evidence: Eleven collections, five authored pages, six policies and the journal.

items.criterion: The crawler file names the machine-readable route list.
items.judgment: The crawler file is read.
items.evidence: A crawler file that names nothing helps nobody.

items.criterion: The home page names the shop.
items.judgment: The home page body is searched for the shop name.
items.evidence: The brand is pinned in the brief.

items.criterion: Every public route and the checkout route answer.
items.judgment: Each declared route is requested.
items.evidence: The route table in the brief.

items.criterion: The account control leads the visitor away rather than into a sign-in the shop does not run.
items.judgment: The handoff route is requested.
items.evidence: The account area is a handoff.

items.criterion: The readiness route answers.
items.judgment: The readiness route is requested.
items.evidence: The deployment contract pins it.

items.criterion: The app root carries the readme, the two reserved directories and the request log.
items.judgment: The paths are read from disk after a request.
items.evidence: The deployment contract pins all four.

items.criterion: The product grid arranges cards of one height in four columns on a wide viewport.
items.judgment: A judge reads a screenshot of the catch-all collection.
items.evidence: The front-end specification pins the grid.

items.criterion: The footer carries four columns ending with the contact column.
items.judgment: A judge reads a screenshot of the footer.
items.evidence: The front-end specification pins the four headings.

items.criterion: The checkout opens as its own route carrying the order summary beside the address form.
items.judgment: A judge walks the cart into the checkout.
items.evidence: The user flow pins the checkout as a route.

items.criterion: The announcement messages at the top of the home route advance one after another on a timed loop.
items.judgment: A judge watches the announcement bar.
items.evidence: The home route rule pins three rotating messages.

items.criterion: Every interactive control reaches a visible focus ring by keyboard.
items.judgment: A judge tabs through the storefront.
items.evidence: The technical requirements pin keyboard reach.

items.criterion: The product grid reflows to two columns on a phone-width viewport.
items.judgment: A judge reads a narrow-viewport screenshot.
items.evidence: The front-end specification pins the breakpoints.

items.criterion: The benefit strip beneath the hero on the home route carries five reassurance devices in one row.
items.judgment: A judge reads the home page beneath the hero.
items.evidence: The home route rule pins five benefits.

items.criterion: The cart drawer opens over the page carrying the lines, the subtotal and the checkout control.
items.judgment: A judge adds a watch and opens the drawer.
items.evidence: The user flow pins the drawer.
